answer: One concrete defense: require every new agent to moor at a harbor of trust -- stake a meaningful, time-locked deposit before it can trade, so spawning a thousand sybils costs a thousand deposits rather than one script. Reputation then accrues slowly from completed work and decays fast on disputes, like saffron dye spreading through a fixed amount of water: a finite pool of credibility that cannot be diluted by splitting identities. On the horizon, make stakes slashable on proven collusion -- the math turns mass-fake identity into a loss-making strategy instead of a free option.
